claims.text: Rapid temperature ramping provides insufficient time for atomic diffusion.
Insufficient atomic diffusion causes local compositional imbalances.
Local compositional imbalances lock in phase separation and elemental segregation.
Local compositional imbalances produce defective or irregular nanoparticle morphologies.
Slower ramp rates near the nucleation temperature provide enough time for more complete atomic diffusion and mixing.
Under slower ramps, high mixing entropy overcomes differences in elemental diffusivity.
Enhanced atomic mixing under slower ramps yields a uniform single-phase solid solution.
The proposed initial system is based on Au, Ag, Pt, Pd, and Cu at a fixed overall composition.
The relevant nucleation range is approximately 200–500 °C.
The nanoscale degree of atomic mixing is governed by the time available for diffusion during the thermal ramps.
Rapid heating and cooling freeze local compositional inhomogeneities into the nanoparticles.
Slower thermal ramps promote homogeneous integration of the constituent elements.
Slower controlled ramps will increase the likelihood of obtaining a single-phase solid solution relative to the rapid-ramp baseline.
Slower controlled ramps will reduce elemental segregation relative to the rapid-ramp baseline.
Slower controlled ramps will produce more controlled, often more spherical, nanoparticle morphologies.
Slower controlled ramps will lower the onset temperature for thermal decomposition.
The rapid-ramp baseline exhibits phase separation, elemental segregation, irregular morphology, and higher thermal-decomposition thresholds.
The proposed mechanism is applicable to compositions based on Au, Ag, Pt, Pd, and Cu when temperature can be precisely controlled around the nucleation window.
The mechanism may not apply to systems having markedly different diffusivities or substantially different processing-temperature ranges.
Failure of slower ramps to produce a statistically significant structural improvement relative to the rapid-ramp control would falsify the proposed ramp-rate mechanism.
